hint.effectiveOpacity in all runs: probe-computed, not the broker value (see probeDefects).
probeDefects: {...hint, effectiveOpacity: parseFloat(hint.style.opacity)} overwrites broker DESCRIBE effectiveOpacity (ancestor product). opacity-control reports 1 although nonDefaultAncestors shows hint-wrapper opacity 0.12. Never overwrite broker fields; use new names.
Uses packet.viewport as an object (string) -> NaN scroll. Read innerHeight from broker 'viewport'.
Only stack[0] is meaningful, and the probe does no occluder classification. It never checks whether the span is stack[0], and it ignores fixed elements and banner rects.

The pixel clip is the span box: glyph pixels are mixed with background and with whatever covers it. No reference clip (unoccluded #777, background-only) and no check that the clip's max pixel is the expected background (255).
Hypothesis predictions are mis-specified: h1 'max<=245', h2 'opacity<1' instead of background alpha.
mostImportantChange: Make the hint's occluder explicit and avoid it by scrolling, with no clicks. After findText, call elementsFromPoint on the hint points. If stack[0] is not the span, read the covering element's rect from the stack (e.g. the fixed banner at y317). Then scrollTo an integer y that puts the hint in the free band above the banner top, e.g. (scrollY + hint.y) - floor((bannerTop - hint.h)/2), clamped to 0..docHeight-innerHeight. Re-run elementsFromPoint and take pixels only when the span (or an element with bg alpha<1) is stack[0]. Otherwise log 'occluded' and skip pixels.
